svg.title: ARC-106 Roof Plan
svg.text: PERGOLA OVER — OPEN, NOT A ROOF
BALCONY +13.20 — 15.7 m², FALLS TO THE EDGE
External / party wall cut by section, 300 mm —
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. The surfaces that shed water, which no other sheet draws:
the roof over the penthouse at +16.45, the terraces and
the open corridor at +13.20, the balcony, and the plant
2. Outlines, parapets, the plant deck and the levels are
measured from the geometry and are exact. The falls and
the outlet positions are architectural intent, drawn so
the drainage package has something to coordinate against.
3. PL-200 and PL-300 set the outlet positions, the pipe
sizes, the downpipe routes and the overflow provision.
Nothing here is a drainage design.
4. Waterproofing turned up 150 mm minimum at every parapet,
upstand and threshold and dressed into the outlet.
Membrane and insulation build-up to the specification.
5. The pergola over the corridor is open and is not a roof:
the corridor under it is an external surface and drains as
one. The stair well is open to the sky under its canopy.
6. The areas here are drainage zones, not the use areas on
A-104, and they divide the same surfaces differently —
hence "north strip" rather than A-104's north terrace,
which also counts the slab north of the stair. The two
differ by 0.17 m²: A-104 deducts the full 2.05 m strip for
the stair well, which is 2.00 m wide.
Preliminary design issue — not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P18 2026-10-07 scheme A adopted: serpentine balcony on every plan; site named
P19 2026-10-07 serpentine waist deepened 0.75 to 1.35 m; 15.7 m² of balcony a floor
P20 2026-10-07 internal partitions 100 mm red brick, specified by the client
P21 2026-10-07 300 mm external and party walls: brick, colour unrestricted
